title: Sell Mineral Rights in Daniel, WY
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Daniel, WY | Sublette County
metaDescription: Daniel, WY sits between the Pinedale gas fields and the Green River headwaters in Sublette County. Get an honest read on your mineral interest before selling.
heroLead: Daniel sits close enough to Pinedale that I always check whether a tract here falls inside the Anticline's productive unit boundary before assuming it's just quiet ranch ground.
intro: This is historic cattle country, site of one of the earliest cattle drives in Wyoming history, but it also sits near enough to the Pinedale Anticline's tight-gas development that some Daniel-area sections do carry real lease and production history. Others, further from the field's core, remain undeveloped acreage that's never drawn operator interest.
I check your exact legal description against the current unit boundary before telling you anything, since the difference between inside and outside the field changes the entire pricing conversation.

sections.heading: Ranch history over a productive gas field
paragraphs: The Green River drainage through this part of Sublette County has been cattle country since before the oil industry existed here, and a lot of Daniel-area mineral interests trace to those original ranch homesteads. What's changed is that some of that ground now sits over, or adjacent to, active Pinedale Anticline tight-gas development.
Determining which situation applies to your family's specific tract is the first and most important step before we discuss any number.

sections.heading: Pricing depends on your exact position
paragraphs: For tracts with real production, I work from your trailing royalty statements and where the underlying wells sit on their decline curve. For undeveloped acreage nearby, I price against comparable recent Sublette County trades. Both are legitimate assets, just priced on entirely different bases.

The Green River Drift, the annual cattle drive route that runs near here, is a reminder of just how long this ground has been worked as ranch land, long before anyone thought about what was underneath it. That history is part of why so many mineral interests here trace to a single original family.

faqs.question: Is Daniel inside the Pinedale Anticline unit?
faqs.answer: Some sections are, others aren't. I'll check your exact legal description before answering for your tract.

faqs.question: My family has ranched this ground for generations. Does that affect the mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No, mineral and surface are separate estates. Ranching history doesn't change mineral ownership, though it often explains how the interest was originally acquired.

faqs.question: What if my royalty checks are inconsistent month to month?
faqs.answer: That's common with tight-gas production and pricing fluctuations. I'll look at your trailing statements as a trend, not a single month.

faqs.question: Can you help even if I don't have the original mineral deed?
faqs.answer: Yes, I can typically reconstruct ownership from the Sublette County recorder's index using a family or ranch name.
